A complete doctrine, command-safeguard, proliferation, and dual-use finding is absent.","closed_system_silence":"High risk: censorship, restricted access, and opaque command structures could conceal dissent, safeguards failures, or misconduct.","duplicate_reporting":"E006 and E018 are one IAEA source-claim unit. E019 and E020 are distinct claims from one ACA source family. Counts must exclude duplicated locators and same-source duplicates.","favorable_and_adverse_search":"Both adverse signaling/safety and contrary restraint/compliance evidence were searched, but coverage remains incomplete across doctrine, safeguards, arms control, proliferation, and dual-use policy.","missing_source_type":"Primary 2022 Russian doctrine and command-safeguard records, technical safeguards material, and precise proliferation or dual-use policy records are missing.","official_claim_independence":"TIME independently reports E005; IAEA, UN, ACA, DoD, and UNODA provide external checks. Internal command interpretations and some official posture claims remain insufficiently verified.","open_system_complaint_volume":"Not a principal risk; secrecy and access limitations matter more than complaint volume.","population_exposure_authority_baseline_shocks":"Putin’s formal authority is documented by AUTH-01, but population exposure, inherited nuclear posture, institutional safeguards authority, and the Ukraine-war shock remain insufficiently separated.","supporting_evidence_ids":["AUTH-01","E004","E005","E006","E007","E019","E020","E035","E036","E047","E048"],"unresolved_risks":["Internal command safeguards remain unverified.","The record remains concentrated on signaling, exercises, diplomacy, and Zaporizhzhia rather than the complete selected nuclear-policy scope."]},"chapter_id":"1B","defensible_evidence_estimate":10,"independent_source_family_estimate":7,"missing_themes":["Primary 2022 doctrine and command-safeguard record","Independent verification of arms-control implementation","Proliferation and dual-use policy","Nuclear governance beyond the cited Zaporizhzhia incident"],"substantive_issues":["Attribution and source-quality gaps remain material, although formal state responsibility is supportable for several policy and facility matters.","E006 and E018 must count as one source-claim unit, not independent evidence."]},{"attribution_risk":"medium","bias_review":{"allegations_vs_findings":"E001-E002 are formal UN resolutions; E003 and E022-E023 report OHCHR findings or documented abuses with stated limits; E021/E039 document access failures, not universal mistreatment; E020/E024/E037/E049 describe negotiations or diplomatic alternatives without proving decision ownership or causation; E038 preserves the distinction between reported violations and adjudicated findings.","closed_system_silence":"High risk: wartime censorship, restricted access, and repression can suppress evidence about civilian harm, detainee treatment, alternatives, and accountability.","duplicate_reporting":"E006 and E018 are one IAEA source-claim unit. E021 and E039 substantially duplicate the same ICRC access claim and count once. E020 and E019 share an ACA family but contain distinct claims. E001 and E002 are distinct UN resolutions.","favorable_and_adverse_search":"Adverse conduct and detention evidence was substantially searched, with contrary Ukrainian-abuse and diplomatic material added. Russian restraint claims, peace initiatives, alternative explanations, proxy/intelligence conduct, and accountability evidence remain incompletely searched or independently checked.","missing_source_type":"Russian and Ukrainian negotiation records, proxy/intelligence evidence, complete POW monitoring, and independent accountability or remedy records are missing.","official_claim_independence":"UN, OHCHR, ICRC, IAEA, and CSIS provide external checks. Russian claims about legitimacy, restraint, and accountability were not independently tested.","open_system_complaint_volume":"International attention may overrepresent visible Ukraine-related harms, while restricted access may undercount less visible conduct and detainee abuse; net bias remains unresolved.","population_exposure_authority_baseline_shocks":"The notebook identifies invasion, mobilization, annexation, occupation, and sanctions shocks, but does not fully distinguish affected populations, inherited conflict conditions, Russian authority, and war effects.","supporting_evidence_ids":["AUTH-01","E001","E002","E003","E006","E007","E020","E021","E022","E023","E024","E037","E038","E039","E049"],"unresolved_risks":["Negotiation failure and decision ownership remain unresolved.","Proxy, intelligence, and accountability coverage remains incomplete.","Attribution is stronger for formal state conduct than for every subordinate battlefield or detention act."]},"chapter_id":"2B","defensible_evidence_estimate":14,"independent_source_family_estimate":9,"missing_themes":["Russian decision records and causal attribution for negotiation failure","Proxy and intelligence conduct","Complete prisoner and detainee monitoring","Accountability and remedy outcomes","Balanced evidence on restraint and civilian-protection claims"],"substantive_issues":["Event coverage improved materially, but causal attribution and contrary-evidence gaps remain.","Local conflict and spending indicators are contextual, not direct ruler evidence."]},{"attribution_risk":"medium","bias_review":{"allegations_vs_findings":"E008 documents Putin’s signature of restrictive laws. E025, E028, and E029 report abuses and systemic conditions with varying attribution strength; E009 is an allegation record. E050 records a prison investigation, but not its outcome or independence. E051 preserves adverse findings and official contrary claims. Effective remedies, corrective action, and tolerated non-state violence remain insufficiently established.","closed_system_silence":"High risk: censorship, foreign-agent pressure, restricted assembly, and weak judicial independence can suppress complaints, detention evidence, and remedies.","duplicate_reporting":"No exact duplicate is identified, but E008, E011, E028, and portions of E029 overlap in repression coverage and must be reconciled by claim rather than treated as wholly independent corroboration. E050 shares the HRW family with E028.","favorable_and_adverse_search":"Adverse searches cover protests, prisons, minorities, and gender-based violence. Some corrective and official contrary material was found, but a systematic search for effective remedies, lawful enforcement, released detainees, and corrective action remains incomplete.","missing_source_type":"Independent prison-monitoring, torture, minority-rights, remedy, and non-state-violence sources with precise 2022 locators are missing.","official_claim_independence":"OHCHR, HRW, OVD-Info, Amnesty, Freedom House, and State Department reporting provide external checks, while E051 records official Russian claims. Verification of those official claims and remedy outcomes remains limited.","open_system_complaint_volume":"Visible protest and opposition cases may exaggerate severity in highly reported settings, while censorship suppresses complaints elsewhere; the direction of net bias is unresolved.","population_exposure_authority_baseline_shocks":"Population groups, regional variation, inherited institutional conditions, and the Ukraine-war shock are not adequately separated. Formal authority supports signed-law attribution, not every subordinate act.","supporting_evidence_ids":["AUTH-01","E008","E009","E010","E011","E025","E027","E028","E029","E050","E051"],"unresolved_risks":["E009 must remain allegation wording.","Effective remedies and positive corrective evidence are sparse.","Country-level priors cannot independently establish Putin’s personal responsibility."]},"chapter_id":"3B","defensible_evidence_estimate":9,"independent_source_family_estimate":7,"missing_themes":["Effective remedies and corrective action","Domestic prison and torture findings with precise locators","Minority and vulnerable-group outcomes","Non-state violence and state tolerance"],"substantive_issues":["Breadth improved, but remedy evidence and attribution for subnational conduct remain unresolved.","Systemic conditions require proportional attribution to formal responsibility, tolerance, or failure to remedy."]},{"attribution_risk":"medium","bias_review":{"allegations_vs_findings":"E008, E026/E040, and E027/E041 document attributable laws, orders, and blocking actions. E009 is an allegation record. E010-E011 and E016 report institutional findings concerning courts, critics, and media. E052 supplies regional-election reporting but does not establish Putin’s personal manipulation of each contest. Judicial-remedy and regional evidence remains incomplete.","closed_system_silence":"High risk: censorship, intimidation, executive influence over courts, and restricted assembly can hide misconduct and make compliance appear stronger than it is.","duplicate_reporting":"E026 and E040 are the same Freedom House source-claim family; E027 and E041 are the same Amnesty source-claim family. E008, E025, E026, E027, and E029 overlap in repression and censorship themes and require claim-level deduplication.","favorable_and_adverse_search":"Adverse institutional and censorship evidence was expanded, and regional-election evidence was added. A balanced search for electoral competition, lawful institutional performance, judicial remedies, regional variation, and corrective action remains incomplete.","missing_source_type":"Election-monitoring and results records beyond the cited regional report, court decisions, independent internet-control measurements, regional evidence, and primary institutional records are missing.","official_claim_independence":"Freedom House, Amnesty, OVD-Info, HRW, OHCHR, Golos, and State Department material provide external checks. Official claims about legality, judicial process, and electoral legitimacy were not independently tested.","open_system_complaint_volume":"Visible opposition and media cases concentrate reporting on repression, while censorship suppresses less visible complaints; regional and population coverage is insufficient to resolve the bias.","population_exposure_authority_baseline_shocks":"National baselines, regional exposure, war-related shocks, and Putin’s formal responsibility versus subordinate implementation are not sufficiently separated.","supporting_evidence_ids":["AUTH-01","ENV-01","ENV-02","E008","E009","E010","E011","E016","E025","E026","E027","E029","E040","E041","E052"],"unresolved_risks":["Election and transfer evidence remains limited, although 2022 was not a federal presidential election year.","Judicial-case, regional, and independent internet-measurement coverage is incomplete.","The source mix remains concentrated on external monitors and repression cases."]},"chapter_id":"4B","defensible_evidence_estimate":11,"independent_source_family_estimate":8,"missing_themes":["Election and transfer evidence relevant to 2022 institutions","Judicial cases, remedies, and corrective action","Regional variation","Independent measurement of internet controls"],"substantive_issues":["Censorship and regional-election coverage improved, but election, remedy, regional, and attribution gaps remain.","Formal responsibility supports national-policy attribution, not every institutional outcome."]},{"attribution_risk":"high","bias_review":{"allegations_vs_findings":"E012-E014 report macroeconomic findings and structural context. E032 documents stabilization measures; E033 and E043 are official self-reports requiring independent verification. E042 is a candidate statistical source lacking a precise extracted figure. E053 and E054 provide official outcome and fiscal records, not direct proof of Putin’s effectiveness or personal ownership.","closed_system_silence":"Medium-high risk: restricted information and weak transparency may conceal distributional harm, budget-execution problems, capture, or policy failure.","duplicate_reporting":"E012 and E032 are distinct claims from the same IMF report and source family. E013 and E014 are distinct World Bank products but may overlap in macroeconomic context. E033 and E043 are distinct official source families; E043 should not be treated as independent corroboration of E033 where themes overlap.","favorable_and_adverse_search":"Both adverse sanctions/contraction evidence and favorable stabilization, transfer, poverty, and fiscal records were searched. Household distribution, implementation, appointments, capture, and independent contrary evidence remain insufficiently covered.","missing_source_type":"Household surveys, distributional and realized-inflation data, budget-execution records, procurement/capture evidence, and appointment or policy-ownership records are missing.","official_claim_independence":"IMF and World Bank provide independent macroeconomic checks. E033 and E043 are official claims without independent verification of delivery or distribution; E053 and E054 are official statistical/fiscal records but do not resolve attribution.","open_system_complaint_volume":"Complaint volume is not the principal issue; aggregate indicators can conceal uneven household hardship and regional exposure rather than exaggerate it.","population_exposure_authority_baseline_shocks":"Sanctions, war, resource dependence, inherited fiscal constraints, aggregate population outcomes, and Putin’s policy authority are not adequately disentangled.","supporting_evidence_ids":["AUTH-01","E012","E013","E014","E032","E033","E042","E043","E053","E054"],"unresolved_risks":["Only macroeconomic, fiscal, poverty, and formal-transfer evidence is present.","Putin-specific attribution for appointments, capture, implementation, and distribution remains unresolved.","Aggregate improvements or contraction cannot establish household welfare or governing effectiveness."]},"chapter_id":"5B","defensible_evidence_estimate":8,"independent_source_family_estimate":6,"missing_themes":["Household distribution, poverty, and realized inflation","Budget execution and implementation outcomes","Appointments and policy ownership","Capture and corruption in economic governance"],"substantive_issues":["The latest round improved outcome and fiscal coverage, but distributional effects and ruler-specific policy ownership remain unresolved.","Rosstat and Bank of Russia records provide outcome context rather than sufficient direct attribution to Putin."]},{"attribution_risk":"high","bias_review":{"allegations_vs_findings":"E015 is an independent WHO assessment of school-health strengths and improvement areas. E012 and E032 provide macroeconomic and social-spending context; E033 is an official self-report; E044 provides a formal execution record; E053 provides poverty statistics. These do not establish Putin-specific delivery, service quality, or welfare outcomes across the selected social-governance scope.","closed_system_silence":"High risk for poverty, housing, sanitation, vulnerable groups, and social-protection delivery because restricted information can suppress service failures and complaints.","duplicate_reporting":"E012 and E032 overlap as claims from one IMF report. E033 and E044 refer to distinct official records but may overlap on social-transfer themes; E043 and E044 are the same Social Fund report and count once for identical claims. Cross-chapter reuse is not independent corroboration.","favorable_and_adverse_search":"Favorable stabilization, school-health, social-transfer, and poverty material was found. A balanced search for adverse household outcomes, service gaps, failed delivery, and corrective action remains incomplete.","missing_source_type":"Household surveys, poverty and inequality data beyond the official figures, health-service delivery records, housing and sanitation evidence, and vulnerable-group or social-protection monitoring are missing.","official_claim_independence":"WHO provides an independent check for school-health services, and IMF provides macroeconomic context. E033 and E044 are official records without independent checks of welfare delivery, implementation, or spending outcomes; E053 is official outcome data.","open_system_complaint_volume":"Complaint volume is not directly available. Aggregate indicators and restricted reporting may understate unequal service failures, while visible crisis reporting may overstate nationally representative severity.","population_exposure_authority_baseline_shocks":"Population distribution, inherited service baselines, regional and vulnerable-group exposure, war and sanctions shocks, and formal versus practical authority remain insufficiently separated.","supporting_evidence_ids":["AUTH-01","E012","E015","E032","E033","E043","E044","E053"],"unresolved_risks":["Evidence remains too narrow for the selected social-governance themes.","Local HDI, health, schooling, and immunization facts are contextual indicators, not direct ruler evidence.","Distributional, service-quality, and independent implementation evidence is absent."]},"chapter_id":"6B","defensible_evidence_estimate":6,"independent_source_family_estimate":5,"missing_themes":["Poverty and inequality","Housing and sanitation","Vulnerable-group outcomes","Social-protection delivery","Independent health and education implementation outcomes"],"substantive_issues":["Poverty and formal transfer evidence improved, but service quality, regional exposure, and independent delivery evidence remain missing.","Social Fund and government records establish formal execution claims, not sufficient independent welfare outcomes or Putin-specific operational management."]},{"attribution_risk":"high","bias_review":{"allegations_vs_findings":"E008 documents Putin’s signature of repression laws. E011, E016, and E025 document institutional or authority-linked repression but do not establish personal assets, beneficial ownership, direct deception, or personal benefit. E030 traces networks and assets without proving Putin owned every asset; E031 is a US sanctions finding, not an adjudicated criminal judgment. E009 remains an allegation record. No new defensible personal-integrity unit was recovered.","closed_system_silence":"Very high risk: censorship, intimidation, restricted media, and weak judicial independence can conceal enrichment, conflicts, coercion, and misconduct.","duplicate_reporting":"E008, E011, E016, and E025 are distinct claims but concentrated in HRW/OVD-Info repression reporting. E030 and E031 are distinct asset-related source families; network evidence must not be duplicated as proof of personal ownership.","favorable_and_adverse_search":"Adverse integrity and repression material was searched. Official disclosure infrastructure and asset-information pages were located, but a meaningful favorable search for disclosures, independent audits, lawful explanations, recusals, corrections, or absence of personal benefit was not completed in a form suitable for evidence.","missing_source_type":"Precise Putin asset declarations, beneficial-ownership and corporate records, appointment/conflict-of-interest records, independent audits, direct evidence of personal benefit or deception, and integrity-investigation outcomes are missing.","official_claim_independence":"External reporting checks repression-related conduct. Treasury provides an official sanctions assessment and OCCRP provides documentary tracing, but ownership interpretations remain contested or unverified; no precise disclosure extract was recovered.","open_system_complaint_volume":"Prominent opposition cases may overrepresent visible complaints, while closed-system suppression likely hides broader misconduct; net bias is unresolved.","population_exposure_authority_baseline_shocks":"The chapter lacks a personal-integrity nexus and separation of inherited corruption conditions, institutional exposure, individual authority, personal benefit, and direct knowledge.","supporting_evidence_ids":["AUTH-01","E008","E009","E011","E016","E025","E030","E031"],"unresolved_risks":["The required personal-integrity nexus remains incomplete.","Network and sanctions evidence must not be converted into proven personal ownership or criminal liability.","Independent verification of assets, appointments, and benefit mechanisms is missing."]},"chapter_id":"7B","defensible_evidence_estimate":7,"independent_source_family_estimate":5,"missing_themes":["Independent verification of Putin-specific ownership or benefit","Appointments and conflicts of interest","Direct deception and disclosures","Audits, corrections, or integrity investigations"],"substantive_issues":["No defensible new personal-integrity unit was recovered in the final pass.","Formal presidential authority and institutional repression evidence cannot substitute for the chapter’s required personal-integrity nexus."]},{"attribution_risk":"high","bias_review":{"allegations_vs_findings":"E001-E002 are formal UN resolutions; E008 is a directly attributable signed-law action; E012-E013 report macroeconomic findings; E020/E024/E037/E049 describe negotiation content; E032 documents stabilization measures; E033-E034/E046 are official records or self-reports requiring independent verification; E043/E045 provide formal social-program execution records; E054 records macro-fiscal outcomes; E055 records formal national-project adaptation without demonstrating success. None establishes a complete portfolio with implementation quality, adaptation, durability, and outcomes.","closed_system_silence":"High risk: censorship and weak institutional independence can hide policy failure, implementation gaps, dissent, and adverse outcomes.","duplicate_reporting":"E001 and E002 are distinct resolutions. E012 and E032 are distinct claims from one IMF report. E013 and E014 are distinct World Bank products. E034 and E046 refer to the same budget-document source family and count once for identical claims. E043 and E045 refer to the same Social Fund report and count once for identical claims. Cross-chapter reuse is not independent corroboration.","favorable_and_adverse_search":"Adverse war, repression, and contraction evidence was partly balanced by stabilization, social-spending, budget, negotiation, fiscal, and adaptation material. A systematic portfolio-level search for achievements, delivery, corrective action, durability, and independent outcome evaluation remains incomplete.","missing_source_type":"Official program portfolios tied to 2022 execution, implementation audits, appointment and ownership records, service-delivery outcomes, and independent effectiveness evaluations are missing.","official_claim_independence":"UN, IMF, World Bank, ACA, CSIS, and IAEA provide independent checks for selected events or outcomes. E033-E034/E046 and E043/E045 are official claims or records without independent implementation verification; E054 and E055 are formal official records but do not resolve ruler attribution or effectiveness.","open_system_complaint_volume":"International attention is concentrated on the Ukraine war and repression, potentially exaggerating those dimensions relative to ordinary governance; censorship may simultaneously hide domestic failures.","population_exposure_authority_baseline_shocks":"Population effects, state capacity, Putin’s formal authority, inherited economic and institutional baselines, and sanctions/war shocks remain insufficiently separated. Aggregate outcomes are inadequate for effectiveness attribution.","supporting_evidence_ids":["AUTH-01","E001","E002","E008","E010","E012","E013","E020","E024","E032","E033","E034","E043","E045","E046","E054","E055"],"unresolved_risks":["No complete 2022 governing-program portfolio is documented.","Implementation quality, adaptation, durability, and independent outcome evaluation remain missing.","War and sanctions materially confound outcome interpretation.","Local capacity indicators remain contextual, not direct evidence of ruler effectiveness."]},"chapter_id":"8B","defensible_evidence_estimate":14,"independent_source_family_estimate":10,"missing_themes":["Complete 2022 governing-program portfolio","Implementation and budget-execution evidence","Appointments and program ownership","Adaptation and corrective action","Durability and independent outcome evaluation"],"substantive_issues":["Formal policy, fiscal, social-program, and adaptation records improved coverage, but portfolio completeness and outcome evaluation remain unresolved.","War and sanctions shocks materially confound effectiveness attribution."]}],"global_findings":["Research rounds were exhausted without full saturation. This is a terminal research conclusion, not a claim that the dossier is complete.","All eight selected chapters retain residual evidence limitations; these should reduce confidence and constrain interpretation, not be treated as negative ruler evidence.","Same-source claims, duplicated locators, and cross-chapter reuse must not inflate defensible evidence or independence estimates; E006/E018, E021/E039, E026/E040, E027/E041, E043/E044/E045, and E034/E046 require claim-level reconciliation.","Favorable and adverse searches were attempted, but contrary, corrective, restraint, and source-type coverage remains uneven, especially for domestic remedies, welfare delivery, personal integrity, and governing effectiveness.","The local-fact disposition is described conceptually, but an explicit audit mapping of each local fact to its permitted contextual use remains absent.","Closed-system silence is a recurring material risk; open-system complaint concentration and war-focused international coverage create additional visibility distortions.","The principal unresolved defects are attribution, missing event and implementation themes, incomplete contrary-evidence searches, limited precise locators for some candidates, and insufficient source-type breadth.","No researcher-written scores, score ranges, anchors, rankings, or null recommendations were found."],"needs_continuation":false,"reviewer_summary":"Terminal evidence-quality review after all permitted research rounds. The dossier contains multiple credible source-claim units with improving source breadth and clearer attribution limits, but every chapter retains material missing themes or unresolved bias. The strongest support concerns formal state actions, documented external events, institutional records, and macro or program context; the weakest areas are personal integrity, domestic remedies, household and service-delivery outcomes, internal nuclear safeguards, negotiation decision ownership, and portfolio-level effectiveness. These unresolved gaps are not negative ruler evidence.","schema_version":"ruler_evidence_review_v1","selected_theme_ids":[]}
